payload.explanation: This log sequence is normal because it consists only of normal-tagged node-discovery and GetNodeInfo no-response messages, a no-topology-change report, temperature notifications, and peer traps. The sequence moves from repeated discovery attempts and no responses to a no-topology-change report, then temperature state notifications interleaved with peer traps. No line is tagged abnormal; the discovery messages, no responses, and temperature notifications are all tagged normal.

This log sequence is normal because all 20 entries are tagged normal and record temperature notices, peer traps, subnet discovery, synchronization, and data-source and MAD activity. The window progresses from temperature warnings and peer traps through subnet rediscovery and an IB node in INIT state, includes a temperature return-to-normal notice, and continues with synchronization and further data-source, MAD, and temperature events. Unlike an abnormal window, it contains no abnormal-tagged entry; the datasource and MAD messages, like the other events, are tagged normal.

This log sequence is normal because it consists only of routine storage, subsystem, network, USB, scheduler, device-mapper, and controller-discovery events. The window moves from system initialization through network setup and USB host-controller registration, with line 7 reporting that no suitable network device was found and a lid base was set. No line is tagged abnormal, distinguishing this sequence from one containing an abnormal-tagged event.

This log sequence is normal because it consists only of routine file-opening log events reporting “Too many open files” and “No such file or directory.” Entries 1–7 report “Too many open files,” entries 8–12 report “No such file or directory,” and entries 13–20 return to “Too many open files.” No entry is tagged abnormal, which distinguishes this window from an abnormal sequence.

No line is tagged abnormal, so despite the reported no-responses and discovery/MAD messages, the sequence contains no abnormal-tagged event supporting the opposite verdict.

No line is tagged abnormal, so the warning notices and datasource no-answer messages do not provide an abnormal-tagged event distinguishing this window from a normal one.
